concerns.text: The spec redefines the aggregation method to simply convert all limits to a common confidence level and select the minimum (most stringent) limit (see FR‑002). The original idea required a statistically rigorous combination (inverse‑variance weighting, heterogeneity assessment, random‑effects modeling). This constitutes a silent drift of the research question from “optimal meta‑analysis of upper bounds” to an easier “pick the smallest bound”, which will not answer the stated scientific question.

The idea explicitly calls for heterogeneity assessment (Cochran’s Q, I²) and, when needed, a random‑effects model to account for systematic differences between experiments. No functional requirement in the spec (FR‑001…FR‑010) addresses this, leaving a gap in required statistical rigor.

FR‑007 mandates a leave‑one‑out cross‑validation on the minimum‑limit aggregation. This analysis was not part of the original idea and, given the drift to a minimum‑limit rule, provides little scientific value and adds unnecessary complexity.

FR‑010 requires a permutation test (10,000 shuffles) on scalar upper‑limit values. Constitution Principle VII specifies permutation testing on polarization‑vs‑momentum data; applying it to a deterministic minimum‑limit statistic is ill‑defined and violates the principle. This is an over‑reach that does not serve the research question.
FR‑008 optionally allows bootstrap resampling, but the idea never proposed bootstrapping. Introducing it without justification expands scope beyond the original research plan.
